thread.title: Apple Stock Downgraded On iPhone Sales Slowdown, Market Saturation | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Downgraded On iPhone Sales Slowdown, Market Saturation | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Another investment bank threw in the towel on Apple stock on Tuesday, saying the iPhone has reached market saturation.
X HSBC downgraded Apple ( AAPL ) to hold from buy and trimmed its 12-month price target to 200 from 205. Analysts at the firm said Apple is too dependent on a single product, the iPhone, which is facing flat sales, CNBC reported .
Apple stock fell 4.4% to close at 176.69 in an overall rough day on the stock market today . It is trading well below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages.
"Apple's iconic hardware unit growth is broadly over for now," HSBC analysts said in a report. "Revenues are only supported by higher selling prices and by the development of services."

Three weeks ago, Guggenheim Securities downgraded Apple to neutral from buy. It said increased average selling prices won't be enough to offset slowing iPhone demand.
Apple Chip Supplier Cirrus Logic Cuts Outlook Late Monday, audio chip supplier Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) slashed its revenue forecast for the current quarter, citing "recent weaknesses in the smartphone market." Cirrus Logic received 82% of its revenue from Apple in the September quarter.
The Austin, Texas-based company now expects revenue for the December quarter of $300 million to $340 million. It previously forecast sales of $360 million to $400 million for its fiscal third quarter .
Cirrus Logic stock sank 1.9% to 37.95 on Tuesday.
Warnings From Others Other Apple component suppliers have warned in recent weeks including Japan Display, Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ), Qorvo ( QRVO ) and Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ).
"Widely publicized iPhone production cuts have echoed through the Apple supply chain," Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer said in a report. He reiterated his perform, or neutral, rating on Cirrus Logic.
Susquehanna Financial Group analyst Christopher Rolland said the size of Cirrus Logic's sales revision was "slightly worse than expected." He kept his positive rating on the stock, but lowered his price target to 43 from 48.
